title: Bootloader fault hardening
question: Does a real bootloader's fault hardening still refuse a tampered image when one instruction is disturbed?

example.name: One tampered image, single modelled faults (details withheld)
example.description: A small harness around a real bootloader's hardening code, run on the RV32 simulator of the firmware module. Details are withheld pending responsible disclosure.
example.command: python3 scripts/run_labs.py  (in the module folder; needs the private notes)

findings.text: Experimental analysis of a real bootloader's fault hardening; details withheld pending responsible disclosure.
findings.label: SIMULATED

labels.MEASURED: counted or computed by running real tools on real inputs in this module
labels.SIMULATED: the outcome of a model (fault simulator or probing model); a model, not silicon
labels.UNTESTED: stated or expected, but not checked by any run in this module yet

caveats: Limits first: a small test harness around the bootloader's hardening code, one compiler, one optimisation setting at a time and one modelled fault, on an instruction simulator. The full bootloader was not compiled.
A result of the model is a reason to look closer, not a proven attack on any device. Related work on this bootloader's hardening has been published by others, so this may already be known.
